name: Datum Plot
tagline: Analyse data and make publication-ready graphs: statistics, regression, curve fitting and page layouts, in one app for Windows.
for: Scientists, researchers, lab teams and students.
about: Datum Plot keeps data, analyses and graphs linked. Type or paste data into a table, choose an analysis, and the results and the graph follow; change a value and everything updates.

It covers the statistics most lab and research work needs, from t-tests and ANOVA to regression and curve fitting, explains each result in plain words with ready methods text, and makes figures ready for a journal: multi-panel layouts at journal sizes, exported as PNG, TIFF, SVG, PDF or EPS. Python runs inside the app, with nothing else to install.

steps.title: Enter the data
steps.text: Choose a table for your kind of data and type, paste or import it (CSV, TXT or .xlsx).

steps.title: Analyse
steps.text: Pick a test or a fit; the results, P values and methods text open on a results sheet linked to the data, and fits are drawn on the graph.

steps.title: Graph and export
steps.text: Style the graph, lay out the figure and export it at journal size.

highlights: A linked chain: data tables → analyses → results → graphs → layouts. Change a value and every result and graph updates.
Data tables for every kind of experiment (XY, groups, two factors, counts, survival, nested, many variables) and worksheets with units and column formulas that update as the data change.

Statistics: descriptive, normality, outliers, t-tests, nonparametric tests, one- and two-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons, nested t-tests and ANOVA, contingency tables, correlation, power, Bland-Altman, ROC, and survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, hazard ratios).

Linear regression and curve fitting with a model library or your own equation, global fits and model comparison; multiple, logistic and Poisson regression, principal components and clustering on tables of many variables.
Matrices and 3D: contour maps, heat maps and 3D surfaces, polar graphs, and surface fits (plane, quadratic, cubic, 2D Gaussian).
Peaks and signals: find peaks above a baseline, fit Gaussian, Lorentzian or Voigt peaks, Fourier spectra and filters.
Materials testing: tensile tests, Weibull strength, Arrhenius activation energies, S–N fatigue curves, and DSC/TGA thermal analysis (onsets, enthalpies, mass loss).
Publication graphs: error bars, axis breaks (XY and column graphs), a second Y axis, annotations, colour-blind-safe colours, multi-panel figures and insets.
Page layouts at journal sizes; export as PNG or TIFF (with CMYK), SVG, PDF or EPS.
Interactive graphs: zoom, pan, drag notes and exclude points with a right-click.
Free and open source (MIT), Windows first, installs in seconds with Python inside, and updates itself.
